title: Limit criterion for local finite presentation of an algebraic stack
statement: Schemes and algebraic spaces are as in [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids on schemes, with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and which has a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. An open substack is a full substack whose pullback by every scheme-valued object is an open subscheme. Smoothness, flatness and local finite presentation of morphisms to schemes are tested after smooth scheme atlases of the source, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$. Then $\mathcal X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation if and only if the following limit condition holds. For every small directed inverse system $(T_i)$ of affine $S$-schemes with affine transition maps and limit $T$, the natural functor $2\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal X(T_i)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is an equivalence of groupoids. Here $\mathcal X(T)$ consists of the objects over $T$ and their isomorphisms; the 2-colimit means objects descend to a stage, isomorphisms descend to a common later stage, and equality of such isomorphisms holds at some later stage whenever it holds over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0CMY, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, specialized to an algebraic stack over a scheme; compared with moduli-curves.tex Tag 0DSS, lemma-curves-qs-lfp.

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. The etale-stack/atlas hypotheses give fppf descent by [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $q:U\to\mathcal X$. By the chart definition in the statement, $U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. The space $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ represents triples $(u,v,\alpha:q(u)\simeq q(v))$. Its projections to $U$ are smooth base changes of $q$ and hence locally of finite presentation; composing with $U\to S$ shows that $R\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Composition in $\mathcal X$ gives composition of these triples. Thus the continuity theorem [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] applies to both $U$ and $R$, over any affine inverse system. In particular it descends maps and detects eventual equality of maps into each of them.

source.place: Tag 0CMX (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-limit-preserving), first paragraph; using the atlas relation directly instead of introducing its quotient.

proof.text: Fix $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ and $x\in\mathcal X(T)$. The atlas base change $U\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$ is smooth surjective. By [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] it has sections after an etale covering of $T$. Such a covering is fppf by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus, def-pc-fppf-site]. The finite affine refinement [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] gives a standard fppf covering $\{V_a\to T\}_{a=1}^m$ with maps $u_a:V_a\to U$ and isomorphisms $q(u_a)\simeq x|_{V_a}$. It is standard because each map between affines is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and is already locally of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-standard-fppf-cover-limit-descent] this covering descends to $\{V_{i,a}\to T_i\}$. Put $V_{j,a}=V_{i,a}\times_{T_i}T_j$ for $j\ge i$. Their pair and triple overlaps are affine, with affine transition maps and respective limits the overlaps of the $V_a$. For example their rings are tensor products over the stage ring, and compatible maps from these tensor products are exactly the compatible pairs of ring maps, which proves the asserted limit identifications.

source.place: Tag 0CMX, standard fppf covering and its descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] to the finitely many $u_a:V_a\to U$, obtaining maps $u_{j,a}:V_{j,a}\to U$ at a common stage. The chosen isomorphisms to $x$ give arrows $r_{ab}:V_a\times_TV_b\to R$ between $u_a$ and $u_b$. Descend these maps by the same theorem. Increase $j$ to make their source and target equal the restrictions of $u_{j,a},u_{j,b}$: these are finitely many equalities of maps into $U$ which hold over the limit. On triple overlaps increase $j$ once more to impose $r_{bc}\circ r_{ab}=r_{ac}$, using eventual equality of maps into $R$. The arrows therefore give an object descent datum for $q(u_{j,a})$ on the fppf covering of $T_j$. Fppf effectiveness, obtained in step 1, gives $x_j\in\mathcal X(T_j)$. Its restriction to $T$ has the original datum; the isomorphism sheaf condition glues the local identifications with $x$ to an isomorphism $x_j|_T\simeq x$. This proves essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0CMX, descent of the finite maps, source/target equations, and cocycle equations.

proof.text: For fullness, let $x_i,y_i\in\mathcal X(T_i)$ and $\alpha:x_i|_T\simeq y_i|_T$. Use [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections, lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] at stage $i$ to choose finite affine fppf coverings lifting each object to $U$. Their pairwise fibre products give a common finite affine fppf covering $\{V_{i,a}\to T_i\}$, by [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], with fixed lifts $u_{i,a},v_{i,a}$ and isomorphisms to $x_i,y_i$. Under these isomorphisms, $\alpha$ over $V_a$ is a map $h_a:V_a\to R$. Descend all $h_a$ to a common stage by [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test]. Eventual equality for maps into $U$ imposes the prescribed source and target. The isomorphisms among the lifts on overlaps of this stage covering give fixed transition arrows $r^x_{ab},r^y_{ab}$ to $R$. Eventual equality into $R$ imposes the finitely many equations $r^y_{ab}h_a=h_br^x_{ab}$ on affine overlaps. The resulting local isomorphisms glue uniquely by fppf sheaf descent to an isomorphism $x_j\simeq y_j$ inducing $\alpha$. For faithfulness choose the same common lift covering for two stage isomorphisms. If they agree on $T$, their finitely many representing maps to $R$ agree at a common later stage by the same continuity theorem. The sheaf condition makes the global isomorphisms equal there. This proves the two remaining clauses of the required equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0CMX, last sentence: explicit morphism descent and eventual equality, replacing the omitted full-faithfulness argument.

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated equivalence for every affine inverse system, and choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $q:U\to\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] this representable morphism is locally of finite presentation. The forward implication of [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test] gives relative object descent for $q$. Given any $u\in U(T)$, essential surjectivity in the hypothesis gives $x_i\in\mathcal X(T_i)$ and $\gamma:q(u)\simeq x_i|_T$. Apply relative object descent for $q$ to $(u,x_i,\gamma)$, obtaining $u_j\in U(T_j)$ whose restriction is $u$ (the fibres of $h_U$ are discrete). Consequently every map $T\to U$ descends to a stage. Apply the reverse implication of [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test] to $h_U\to h_S$: it is representable by schemes, and its relative object condition is exactly this map-descent assertion, since over $S$ the target fibre has its unique object and identity arrow. Thus $U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. The smooth-atlas definition in the item now says precisely that $\mathcal X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, as required.
